after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
What is the minor of ${a}_{12}$ in the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -3d & 5b \\ b & {c}^{2} & b-d \\ b & -10c & b+d\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we remove the first row and second column:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}∗ & -3d & ∗ \\ b & ∗ & b-d \\ b & ∗ & b+d\end{aligned}]
$$

Next, we calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}b & b-d \\ b & b+d\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}b & b-d \\ b & b+d\end{aligned}| \\  & =b\cdot (b+d)-(b-d)\cdot b \\  & ={b}^{2}+bd-{b}^{2}+db \\  & =2bd\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Given that the minor of ${d}_{12}$ is $-4$, find all the possible values of $p$ in the matrix

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}{p}^{2} & {p}^{3} & 6 \\ -6 & 7 & 5 \\ 5 & 2+p & p-1\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we remove the first row and second column:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}∗ & {p}^{3} & ∗ \\ -6 & ∗ & 5 \\ 5 & ∗ & p-1\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${d}_{12}$ is

 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}-6 & 5 \\ 5 & p-1\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}-6 & 5 \\ 5 & p-1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-6\cdot (p-1)-5\cdot 5 \\  & =-6p-19.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${d}_{12}$ is $-4$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}-6p-19 & =-4 \\ -6p & =15 \\ p & =-\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $p=-\frac{5}{2}.$

Question 2

Given that the minor of d12 is −4, find all the possible values of p in the matrix D=[p2p36−67552+pp−1].

a
p=7
b
p=9
c
p=−2
d
p=−52
e
p=65
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we remove the first row and second column:

D=[∗p3∗−6∗55∗p−1]

The minor of d12 is

det[−655p−1]=|−655p−1|=−6⋅(p−1)−5⋅5=−6p−19.

We're told that the minor of d12 is −4, so we must have:

−6p−19=−4−6p=15p=−52

Therefore, the solution is p=−52.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that the minor is -6(p-1)-25=-6p-19. Equating it to -4 gives p=-5/2; substituting yields 15-19=-4. Thus option d is correct.

content.knowledge_point: Solving for an Unknown Given the Value of a Minor
content.problem:
Given that the minor of ${d}_{12}$ is $-4$, find all the possible values of $p$ in the matrix

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}{p}^{2} & {p}^{3} & 6 \\ -6 & 7 & 5 \\ 5 & 2+p & p-1\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we remove the first row and second column:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}∗ & {p}^{3} & ∗ \\ -6 & ∗ & 5 \\ 5 & ∗ & p-1\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${d}_{12}$ is

 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}-6 & 5 \\ 5 & p-1\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}-6 & 5 \\ 5 & p-1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-6\cdot (p-1)-5\cdot 5 \\  & =-6p-19.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${d}_{12}$ is $-4$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}-6p-19 & =-4 \\ -6p & =15 \\ p & =-\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $p=-\frac{5}{2}.$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Given that the minor of ${m}_{21}$ is $11$, find all the possible values of $y$ in the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}y & \frac{3}{2} & y \\ 25 & 4-y & 12y \\ y & 2 & -6y\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and first column:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}∗ & \frac{3}{2} & y \\ 25 & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & 2 & -6y\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${m}_{21}$ is

 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2} & y \\ 2 & -6y\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2} & y \\ 2 & -6y\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot (-6y)-y\cdot 2 \\  & =-11y.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${m}_{21}$ is $11$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}-11y & =11 \\ y & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y=-1.$
